subject.title: feat: provider fallback by failure class — quarantine auth-broken providers

question: Should OpenClaw make auth-broken provider/profile quarantine a default runtime policy, and what exact signals should distinguish hard auth failure from transient refresh or provider-side 401 noise?
rationale: Current main has partial opt-in and narrow fixes, but making quarantine default affects provider routing, session recovery, status output, and compatibility-sensitive auth behavior.

options.title: Approve bounded default quarantine
options.body: Implement default quarantine only for high-confidence hard-auth signals, add transient-401 confirmation, and expose redacted provider health/status with focused upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep quarantine opt-in for now
options.body: Leave the existing default-off skip cache and handle only narrower proven bugs such as Codex refresh timeout or Anthropic restart loops until more live evidence arrives.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Close or pause the broad policy issue only after moving the remaining Anthropic restart, Codex refresh, and transient retry work into explicit owner-approved issues.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded default quarantine
recommendation.body: Implement default quarantine only for high-confidence hard-auth signals, add transient-401 confirmation, and expose redacted provider health/status with focused upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete handled the maintainer rewrite and landing of the current fallback-skip/auth recovery path and is the clearest routing owner from the current history.
